endorsements.quote: Designers should consider incorporating an implementation science framework early in the development process to not only ensure a user-centered design but to inform how tools are integrated into existing clinical research workflows.

Targets such as leadership engagement, knowledge and beliefs about a tool, the adaptability of a tool, and the planning around implementation all illustrate the importance of a preliminary intake process during which design and study teams can align on knowledge, design needs, and workflow integration.

unlisted_practices: Design AI clinical trial screening tools to be customizable to each study's eligibility criteria, screening priorities, and workflows.
Provide line of sight to where the algorithm identified each eligibility criterion.
Use modular design, common data models, and application programming interfaces at natural joints so AI tools can be upgraded without a complete rebuild.
Design AI tools for generalizability and reusability across trials and integration with electronic medical records and electronic source databases.
Incorporate common screening strategies such as gatekeeper criteria into how AI tools prioritize and display potential subjects.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper that synthesizes key implementation science themes and provides recommendations for designing and rolling out AI-enabled clinical trial screening platforms.
